fixes.explanation: Good guess, friend, but Paul doesn't mention Jerusalem here at all. He says his apostleship is "…by the command of God our Savior and of Christ Jesus our hope…" (1 Timothy 1:1). Paul opens this letter by naming God our Savior and Christ Jesus. That's the whole source he gives.

Close, friend, but this letter says Ephesus: "…you should stay on at Ephesus…" (1 Timothy 1:3). Paul had left for Macedonia, and Timothy was to stay put in Ephesus. Corinth isn't named anywhere in these verses.

Not this one, friend. The verse says Timothy should "…stay on at Ephesus…" (1 Timothy 1:3). Paul says he left for Macedonia, and Timothy was to stay in Ephesus. Antioch doesn't show up in these verses.

Not quite, friend. Nothing in these verses says these men refused to work. Paul says Timothy should instruct them "…not to teach false doctrines" (1 Timothy 1:3). Their teaching is the trouble here, not their work ethic, and I'd say that's a much bigger deal than a long lunch break.

Not in this passage, friend. Food offered to idols never comes up in these verses. Here Paul says Timothy should instruct certain men "…not to teach false doctrines" (1 Timothy 1:3). The false teaching is what he names.

Yes, friend, False. Paul says "They want to be teachers of the law, but they do not understand what they are saying or that which they so confidently assert." (1 Timothy 1:7). They want to teach the law, but they don't understand what they're saying. And they say it with confidence anyway!
You got it, friend. Paul says "…the law is good, if one uses it legitimately." (1 Timothy 1:8). Good is his word for the law. What matters is that it's used the legitimate way.
That's not what Paul says here, friend. He says "…the law is good, if one uses it legitimately." (1 Timothy 1:8). Good is his word for it. Nothing in these verses says it has been done away with.

Not this time, friend. Paul never mentions elders' traditions in these verses. He says sound teaching "…agrees with the glorious gospel of the blessed God…" (1 Timothy 1:10-11). The gospel is the yardstick, and no tradition gets to hold the tape measure.

True, friend! Paul says the glorious gospel is the one "…with which I have been entrusted." (1 Timothy 1:11). Being handed something that important is a big deal. I think Paul felt the weight of that.
Not quite, friend, it's True. Paul says the glorious gospel is the one "…with which I have been entrusted." (1 Timothy 1:11). He didn't make it up. It was put into his hands.
